title: Welcome to the Donald E. Crabtree Lithic Technology Collection
text:
The University of Idaho Library invites you to explore the Donald E. Crabtree Lithic Technology website, meant to illuminate Crabtree’s pioneering stone tool research and to elevate Native and Indigenous knowledge and practices in conversation with the collection.

Crabtree (1912-1980), an Idahoan, devoted his life to the study of stone tools made by humans. He was instrumental in the establishment of the field of experimental archaeology, and his An Introduction to Flintworking (1972) remains the authoritative reference on lithic technology research.

At his death, Crabtree bequeathed his collection to the University of Idaho, where the Alfred W. Bowers Laboratory of Anthropology holds it. In 2021, the UI Library and the Bowers Lab received a CLIR grant to digitize and share the collection. This website provides access to a selection of its roughly 8,000 stone tools and flintknapping samples, including 3,154 artifacts created or collected by Crabtree and others, as well as 4,387 archival photos, correspondence, and research materials.

title: About Donald Crabtree
text: Donald Crabtree's passion and life long dedication to learning flintworking techniques helped establish the field of experimental archaeology. Read about his biography and legacy in our Crabtree legacy section.

title: Crabtree Archives
text: Explore thousands of digitized photographs, slides, and documents from the archives that provide unique insight into Donald Crabtree's lifelong work with lithic technology.

title: Crabtree Flintknapping
text: Discover images and 3D models of over 3,000 stone tools and flintknapping samples created by Donald Crabtree. This represents a small selection of artifacts of the Crabtree Lithic Technology Collection, held by the Alfred W. Bowers Laboratory of Anthropology.

title: Learn About Flintknapping
text: Find videos, books, websites, and other resources about flintknapping on our Learn page. Included are videos from experts and educational booklets from the Bowers Lab.

title: Native Perspectives
text: Hear from an Advisory Board of Native and Indigenous artists, researchers, and scholars discussing topics related to the digitization of lithic artifacts and the presentation of Native and Indigenous provenanced artifacts.

title: 3D Models
text: The digital collection contains over one hundred detailed 3D models of lithic artifacts created using photogrammetry. Visit an item's page and click the 'View 3D Model' to open the interactive viewer directly in your web browser.
